summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9), restricted cron scheduling to root and opsadmin by creating /etc/cron.allow containing only those two users. Since opsadmin did not previously exist, created it first. Verified enforcement (allowed users can use crontab, others are rejected with 'not allowed to use this program'). Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id and cron state, rebooted node1 via `shutdown -r now`, confirmed the node went unreachable then came back, verified the boot_id changed (0d6209e2... -> ece1d32b...), and confirmed crond was active and /etc/cron.allow / opsadmin's ability to schedule cron jobs (and a new test user's inability to) persisted after reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected OS, existing cron.allow/cron.deny, and crond status on node1
Created opsadmin user via useradd (opsadmin did not previously exist)
Verified opsadmin and root can use crontab; created and tested a throwaway user (crontestuser) confirming it is denied cron access
Cleaned up test crontab entries and removed crontestuser
Captured baseline boot_id and cron-access state on node1
Issued 'shutdown -r now' as a backgrounded/acknowledged command so the ack returned before disconnection
Verified boot_id changed, confirming an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified crond active, /etc/cron.allow persisted, opsadmin can schedule cron jobs, and a newly created test user (crontestuser2) is denied
Cleaned up post-restart test artifacts (crontestuser2, opsadmin's test crontab entry)

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: /etc/cron.allow set to root+opsadmin; opsadmin and root can use crontab (rc=0), crontestuser is denied with 'not allowed to use this program'
opsadmin created via useradd, uid=1001 confirmed

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (crond active, cron.allow content, boot identity)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 0d6209e2-350d-4cd9-8a7d-11f7c08072be, crond active, cron.allow=root/opsadmin, opsadmin exists
shutdown -r now issued via backgrounded/disowned sudo command, ack rc=0 returned

evidence.requirement: Node became unreachable then recovered (single node, sequential)
evidence.summary: SSH timed out twice during reboot, then succeeded once node1 came back

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id ece1d32b-f9e7-4cfa-adef-68902fc82224 differs from baseline 0d6209e2-...; uptime -s shows a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: cron access control persisted and enforced
evidence.summary: crond active, /etc/cron.allow unchanged (root/opsadmin), opsadmin successfully schedules a cron job (rc=0) via sudo -u, new test user crontestuser2 denied crontab access
